content:
Apple has revealed further details about the artificial intelligence (AI) labelling rules it announced for Apple Music back in March. Here are the details.

On Apple Music, AI-generated content will be clearly labelled

Earlier this year, Apple announced that Apple Music would soon require AI transparency disclosures for new cover art, songs, compositions, and music videos uploaded to the platform.

Now, the company has further explained how it will work.

In an email sent to creators today, Apple stated that "later this year, we will also make these disclosures visible to Apple Music users through a 'Made With AI' label."

Apple also clarified which situations require disclosure. The email mentioned:

Apple Music added that the aim of this measure is to "provide maximum transparency to listeners as much as possible," and asked creators to refer to their Music Style Guide for more information.

Apple Music's move is only the latest example of streaming platforms responding to the influx of AI-generated music, as more and more musicians incorporate generative AI into their production processes.

Spotify previously stated that it would, by default, exclude music from AI Personas from its editorial and algorithmic recommendations; Deezer announced last year that songs fully generated by AI would not appear in its recommendations and editorial playlists. Deezer also disclosed last month that music fully generated by AI had surpassed 50% of daily new song uploads for the first time.

On the Apple Music side, the platform's head Oliver Schusser previously appeared on Billboard's On the Record podcast, during which he mentioned that although more than one-third of the music uploaded to Apple Music each month is fully AI-generated, it accounts for less than 0.5% of listens on the platform.
